explanation: The first code walks the matrix in the order it is stored: a 64-byte line of the cache serves sixteen elements in a row, so a line is missed once and then used fifteen more times. The second jumps a whole row ahead on every step, and once a column no longer fits the cache almost every element is a miss - 10 instructions of the score for an L1 miss and 100 for an L2 miss. Both loops execute the same instructions; the order of the memory accesses alone makes the walk by columns several times more expensive.

benchmark.inputDescription: Matrices of 768 x 768 and 1024 x 1024 ints, larger than the 1 MiB L2 cache of the model
